pr_title: Require email_verified to be used when email is set as username via CEL
pr_body:
/kind feature
/kind api-change
/assign liggitt aramase 
/triage accepted
/milestone v1.30
/sig auth

Fixes #123675

```release-note
When configuring a JWT authenticator:

If username.expression uses 'claims.email', then 'claims.email_verified' must be used in
username.expression or extra[*].valueExpression or claimValidationRules[*].expression.
An example claim validation rule expression that matches the validation automatically
applied when username.claim is set to 'email' is 'claims.?email_verified.orValue(true) == true'.
```

xref: #130875

issue_context.title: Document `email_verified` check when CEL expression is used in authentication configuration
issue_context.body:
When the `email` claim is used directly, we perform a custom check against the `email_verified` claim if it is present:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9043ce05c125091c0cb5519206fd90d311abd8c8/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/plugin/pkg/authenticator/token/oidc/oidc.go#L779-L793

I do not think this type of check makes sense via the CEL based config, but we should document how to perform a similar validation since that check is lost if moving a config to use CEL expressions and the admin is unaware of the implicit `email_verified` check.

cc @aramase @liggitt
comments:
> I do not think this type of check makes sense via the CEL based config, but we should document how to perform a similar validation since that check is lost if moving a config to use CEL expressions and the admin is unaware of the implicit `email_verified` check.

I think I agree. Should we go so far as to warn or forbid a cel username expression that contains `claims.email` and doesn't contain `claims.email_verified`?

Also, our doc looks misleading up here:
```
	//   Nested claims can be accessed using dot notation, e.g. 'claims.email.verified'.
```

I would never expect an `email` claim to be a nested structured claim... probably better to put a different field in the example.

> Should we go so far as to warn or forbid a cel username expression that contains `claims.email` and doesn't contain `claims.email_verified`?

As in, if your `AuthenticationConfiguration.jwt[N].claimMappings.username.expression` contains the substring `claims.email`, we would require that at least one `AuthenticationConfiguration.jwt[N].userValidationRules[...].expression` contains the substring `claims.email_verified`?  I am not sure if warning is worth the effort (I do not think anyone would actually see it).  Forbidding it seems okay since the CEL validation check is not hard to write and we already require that exact behavior in the existing non-CEL code path?  I guess that question remains: does someone using CEL actually want to perform such a check?

> Also, our doc looks misleading up here

Yeah, will fix.

> I am not sure if warning is worth the effort (I do not think anyone would actually see it). Forbidding it seems okay since the CEL validation check is not hard to write and we already require that exact behavior in the existing non-CEL code path? I guess that question remains: does someone using CEL actually want to perform such a check?

if we start with forbidding .email without doing *something* with .email_verified in some check, that seems safer / nicer / probably correct

review_comments:
I'll trust the unit tests and @jpbetz's review of the traversal logic / comparison with the CEL visitor for correctness.

My only comment all the way down the chain is that it's not obvious which of the fields can be nil, and where the visitor currently works but would panic if it got an AST that was valid but unexpected.

Two ways to resolve that:
1. know for sure what can / can't be nil (now or in the future with any possible future AST changes)
2. check everything that can be nil for nil explicitly

Could you add [integrations tests](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/integration/apiserver/oidc/oidc_test.go#L561) using `claims.email_verified` in
1. username.expression
2. extra[*].valueExpression
3. claimValidationRules[*].expression
I can though we can only cover the positive cases since the API server won't start on the negative cases.
I don't feel strongly about unit or integration tests as long as the unit tests actually exercise the functional evaluator
Opened #123825, will handle this in a follow-up due to limited time left in the release.
This need to be added in `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/apis/apiserver/v1beta1/types.go` as well
cc @jpbetz or @cici37 for review of cel AST traversal

For reference, here's how we statically checked if a CEL expression accesses the `oldSelf` variable for transition rules: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a5f5f44157c49fdfb6384862c7cb34c2ddbd4cce/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/schema/cel/compilation.go#L218-L229

This case is different because it's not just checking if a root variable is referenced, so I don't know if the same approach can work here. But I just wanted to check if this approach has been explored and rejected?
@jpbetz that only shows `claims` as being used (the expression was `claims.email.trim()`):

Gotcha. Can we leverage [`Visitor()`](https://github.com/google/cel-go/blob/9775e65f751b9d2e04d8f942f832de889ec3fb14/common/ast/navigable.go#L139) to avoid reimplementing [visit](https://github.com/google/cel-go/blob/9775e65f751b9d2e04d8f942f832de889ec3fb14/common/ast/navigable.go#L194)?

@jpbetz so I gave that a shot and encountered a few issues:

- Requires cel-go to be bumped to v0.18.0 since that is the earliest tag with the visitor code
- The bump adds/changes a lot of code, and a few places in the code stop compiling in ways that is not super obvious how to fix (I hacked around this)
- The AST type we have contains a private AST implementation type, which is actually what we need to use the visitor.  There doesn't appear to be any clean way for me to get to the underlying type (I also hacked around this)

The visitor code does appear to work, but the other issues make it a rather unsafe choice this late in the release cycle.
Thanks for trying. We'll circle back on this one.

Hi @enj, we shifted over to using the `ast` package so you can avoid the direct proto dep:

```go
root := ast.NavigateAST(resultAST.NativeRep())
matches := ast.MatchDescendents(root, <matcher>)
if len(matches) > 0 { ... }
``` 

The `cel/folding.go` implementation is a pretty good reference point for navigating expressions.

It looks like we would need `v0.18.2` to use the `NativeRep` method.  Either way I think we will have to wait to bump the dep until next release.  I will take a look into `cel/folding.go` and make sure my approach lines up with it.
